# midi_baggies

## What it is

An open-topped tray with four full-height walls, rounded at the corners, and a
window cut into the front wall so a stack of bags can be reached and pulled out
sideways instead of lifted from above. The side walls run full height all the way
to the front corners; only the front wall is notched, and only across its middle.
The cavity floor ramps up near the front to meet the bottom of that opening flush,
so there's no lip for an item to catch on while it's being slid out.

## Design notes

Proportions are taste, not fit, and are plain sliders: `length`, `width`, `height`,
`front_height`, `gap_fraction`, `corner_radius`. Nothing here mates with a
manufactured part, so none of it is measured.

`gap_fraction` sets the opening's width as a fraction of the box's own width,
centered on the front wall, leaving a solid pillar of wall on each side that
blends into the rounded front corners. The cut only punches through the front
wall's own thickness; the side walls are never touched.

`ramp_length` sets how far back from the front the floor's slope reaches before
levelling out to the ordinary flat floor. The rise is not a separate slider: it's
always exactly `front_height`, so the ramp's peak lands flush with the opening's
lower edge with no step. A shorter `ramp_length` makes a steeper ramp; a longer one
a gentler, more gradual one.

`ramp_radius` bows the ramp into a shallow curve instead of a flat slope, using a
true circular arc between the same two endpoints the straight ramp used (so
`ramp_length` and `front_height` still mean exactly what they say). Set it to 0 for
the original flat ramp.

## Don't

- Don't extend the front cut into the side walls. An earlier version lowered the
  side walls near the front too (a wraparound scoop), which also put sliver chamfer
  faces at the step-meets-corner points. Keeping the side walls full height and
  cutting only a window in the front is the simpler shape.
- Don't drop `gap_fraction` close to 1 without also shrinking `corner_radius`: the
  part refuses to build if the wall left beside the opening is too thin once the
  corner rounding eats into it.
- The ramp's extra material in the front sill is also what keeps that area above
  the printer's minimum wall thickness. Don't thin the ramp down without
  rechecking that.
- Don't drop `ramp_radius` below the floor this part's math works out for the
  current `ramp_length`/`front_height` (the refusal message names the number).
  A smaller radius swings the curve down through the floor and splits the ramp
  into a detached sliver instead of one solid.
- Don't try rounding the ramp by filleting the corner where it lifts off the
  floor instead of using the arc. The corner is acute enough that any useful
  radius eats nearly the whole ramp length and reads to the overhang checker as
  a long, nearly-flat unsupported shelf, even sitting right on the floor.
